body.v: Your latest claim statement is available. You'll find it in the HelvetiCare app, under Documents.
We never send statements by email, and we will never ask for your bank details this way.

hotspots.explain: The address ends in helveticare.example, the insurer's real domain.
No request: it only tells you where to find the document.
The insurer states in black and white that it never asks for bank details by email.
A plain subject line: no amount, no deadline.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Read the address, not just the name.
who.answer: HelvetiCare: the address is on helveticare.example.
choices: A broker wanting to sell you a policy

emotion.prompt: Which feeling is this email pressing on?
emotion.answer: None. A plain notice, with no pressure.

ask.prompt: What does it actually want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing, apart from reading your statement in the app if you want to.
choices: Nothing, except reading it in the app
Click a link and sign in

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself, under Documents. The email doesn't suggest anything else anyway.
choices: Reply and ask for the statement
Call the number given in the email

actions.label: Open the HelvetiCare app yourself and read the statement
actions.consequence: The statement is there. The email was only a heads-up.

actions.label: Ignore the email: you'll read the statement later
actions.consequence: No rush: the statement stays available in the app.

actions.label: Reply with your account number to get refunded faster
actions.consequence: The email said the insurer never asks for it. Bank details don't go by email, even to a genuine sender.

attacker_reveal: You can put your suspicions away: this one really is from the insurer. No link, and it tells you itself that it never asks for bank details. Compare it with the email promising a refund: same company, opposite request.
